contrast.method: Opaque sRGB source colors; linearized channels using threshold 0.04045, luminance weights 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722, ratio=(lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05). Nominal text colors, not antialiased edge pixels.

selected_cue.text: Selected candidate is rasterized bold; unselected candidate is regular. Selected number is blue and selected candidate text is dark blue.
selected_cue.shortcut_mapping: Renderer uses input.page_range() and numbers index-range.start+1; numeric shortcuts are never elided.

layout.precision_note: MARGIN=20 controls left/right padding; it is not a claim of four equal 20px margins. Header begins at y=18 and candidate row leaves 18px below it.
layout.font: Font::new("") uses the available font/fallback; no specific Google font is claimed.

screenshot.visual_assessment: Compact light surface, clear two-row hierarchy, restrained blue selected item and ample horizontal whitespace. Candidate text and shortcut numbers are legible; no visible crop, overlap or black alpha corners in this screenshot.

submission_contract.conclusion: Visual elision does not replace or truncate the committed candidate string. Existing frontend byte-capacity rejection remains explicit and preserves editable composition.

limitations: Scope is this candidate popup and existing XIM screenshot; this is not complete Material Design or accessibility certification.
The 20px margin statement applies horizontally. Thin card borders/dividers are decorative and were not substituted for text contrast checks.

Existing evidence separately tests bounded rendering and complete commits; it does not contain a dedicated render-then-commit long-candidate GUI scenario. Immutable rendering input plus unchanged commit path and existing exact-byte tests support the conclusion.
Wayland first-character protocol issue is separately owned by Core; UI review passing is not approval to mark the whole draft ready.
